Get behavioral data\n208\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n209\t    bp = f['obj']['bp']\n210\t    Ntrials = int(bp['Ntrials'][0, 0])\n211\t    \n212\t    L = bp['L'][:].flatten()  # left trials\n213\t    R = bp['R'][:].flatten()  # right trials\n214\t    hit = bp['hit'][:].flatten()  # correct trials\n215\t    miss = bp['miss'][:].flatten()  # error trials\n216\t    no = bp['no'][:].flatten()  # ignore/no-response trials\n217\t    autowater = bp['autowater'][:].flatten()  # WC trials\n218\t    early = bp['early'][:].flatten()  # early lick trials\n219\t    stim_enable = bp['stim']['enable'][:].flatten()  # stimulation trials\n220\t    \n221\t    # Event times\n222\t    goCue = bp['ev']['goCue'][:].flatten()\n223\t    \n224\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n225\t    # 2. Find valid trials\n226\t    # Exclude: early lick, ignore/no-response, stimulation\n227\t    # Include: hit and miss trials\n228\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n229\t    valid_mask = (early == 0) & (no == 0) & (stim_enable == 0) & ((hit == 1) | (miss == 1))\n230\t    valid_trials = np.where(valid_mask)[0]  # 0-indexed\n231\t    \n232\t    if len(valid_trials) < 2:\n233\t        print(f'    Skipping {session_id}: only {len(valid_trials)} valid trials')\n234\t        f.close()\n235\t        return None\n236\t    \n237\t    print(f'    Trials: {Ntrials} total, {len(valid_trials)} valid ({np.sum(hit[valid_trials]==1)} hit, {np.sum(miss[valid_trials]==1)} miss)')\n238\t    \n239\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n240\t    # 3. Process neural data for each probe\n241\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n242\t    all_trialdat = []  # Will be list of (n_timebins, n_neurons, n_all_trials) per probe\n243\t    all_cluid = []     # cluster indices used per probe\n244\t    \n245\t    for probe_num in probes:\n246\t        # Determine correct clu index\n247\t        # If clu has only 1 entry (shape (1,x)), always use index 0\n248\t        # If clu has multiple entries, use probe_num-1 as index\n249\t        clu_shape = f['obj']['clu'].shape\n250\t        if clu_shape[0] == 1:\n251\t            probe_idx = 0\n252\t        else:\n253\t            probe_idx = probe_num - 1\n254\t        \n255\t        # Get clu data for this probe\n256\t        clu_ref = f['obj']['clu'][probe_idx, 0]\n257\t        clu_group = f[clu_ref]\n258\t        \n259\t        # Get cluster qualities\n260\t        qualities = get_cluster_qualities(f, clu_group)\n261\t        n_total_clusters = len(qualities)\n262\t        \n263\t        # Find clusters to use (quality filter)\n264\t        cluid = find_clusters(qualities, PARAMS['quality_exclude'])\n265\t        print(f'    Probe {probe_num}: {n_total_clusters} total clusters, {len(cluid)} after quality filter')\n266\t        \n267\t        if len(cluid) == 0:\n268\t            continue\n269\t        \n270\t        # Align spikes to goCue and bin\n271\t        # For each cluster, get spike times aligned to goCue\n272\t        trialdat = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, len(cluid), Ntrials), dtype=np.float32)\n273\t        \n274\t        for ci, clu_idx in enumerate(cluid):\n275\t            # Get spike times and trial assignments\n276\t            tm_ref = clu_group['trialtm'][clu_idx, 0]\n277\t            trial_ref = clu_group['trial'][clu_idx, 0]\n278\t            \n279\t            spike_trialtm = f[tm_ref][:].flatten()  # spike times relative to trial start\n280\t            spike_trial = f[trial_ref][:].flatten().astype(int)  # 1-indexed trial numbers\n281\t            \n282\t            # Get absolute spike times for alignment\n283\t            tm_abs_ref = clu_group['tm'][clu_idx, 0]\n284\t            spike_tm_abs = f[tm_abs_ref][:].flatten()\n285\t            \n286\t            # Align to goCue: trialtm_aligned = trialtm - goCue(trial)\n287\t            # But we need to compute aligned times\n288\t            # In MATLAB: obj.clu{prbnum}(clu).trialtm_aligned = obj.clu{prbnum}(clu).trialtm - event\n289\t            # where event = obj.bp.ev.goCue(obj.clu{prbnum}(clu).trial)\n290\t            \n291\t            # Compute aligned spike times\n292\t            valid_spike_mask = (spike_trial >= 1) & (spike_trial <= Ntrials)\n293\t            spike_trial_valid = spike_trial[valid_spike_mask]\n294\t            spike_trialtm_valid = spike_trialtm[valid_spike_mask]\n295\t            \n296\t            # goCue times for each spike's trial\n297\t            spike_goCue = goCue[spike_trial_valid - 1]  # 0-index into goCue\n298\t            spike_aligned = spike_trialtm_valid - spike_goCue\n299\t            \n300\t            # Bin spikes for each trial\n301\t            for trial_num in range(1, Ntrials + 1):\n302\t                trial_mask = spike_trial_valid == trial_num\n303\t                if not np.any(trial_mask):\n304\t                    continue\n305\t                \n306\t                trial_spikes = spike_aligned[trial_mask]\n307\t                \n308\t                # Histogram\n309\t                counts, _ = np.histogram(trial_spikes, bins=EDGES)\n310\t                \n311\t                # Smooth: convert to firing rate then smooth\n312\t                fr = counts / PARAMS['dt']  # spks/sec\n313\t                fr_smooth = causal_gaussian_smooth(fr, PARAMS['smooth'], PARAMS['bctype'])\n314\t                \n315\t                trialdat[:, ci, trial_num - Extract trial-level behavioral variables\n359\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n360\t    lick_direction = R.copy()  # 1=right, 0=left\n361\t    context = 1 - autowater  # DR=1, WC=0 (autowater=1 means WC)\n362\t    outcome = hit.copy()  # 1=correct, 0=incorrect\n363\t    \n364\t    # -------------------------------------------------------\n365\t    # 6. neural_trials.append(trialdat[:, :, trial_idx].T.astype(np.float32))  # (neurons, time)\n395\t        \n396\t        trial_info.append({\n397\t            'lick_direction': Done: {n_neurons} neurons, {len(valid_trials)} trials, {elapsed:.1f}s')\n419\t    \n420\t    result = {\n421\t        'neural_trials': neural_trials,\n422\t        'trial_info': trial_info,\n423\t       else:\n630\t                            x = ts_data[paw_idx, 0, :]\n631\t                            y = ts_data[paw_idx, 1, :]\n632\t                    else:\n633\t        # For non-tongue: smooth with window 1 (no-op) and fill missing\n643\t                    fx = interp1d(aligned_times[valid], x[valid], bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)\n644\t                    fy = interp1d(aligned_times[valid], y[valid], bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)\n645\t                    xp = fx(taxis)\n646\t                    yp = fy(taxis)\n647\t                    \n648\t                    # Fill missing with nearest\n649\t                    mask = ~np.isnan(xp)\n650\t                    if np.any(mask):\n651\t                        from scipy.interpolate mask = ~np.isnan(yp)\n655\t                    if np.any(mask):\n656\t                        yp = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], yp[mask])\n657\t                    \n658\t                    xpos[:, trix] = xp\n659\t                    ypos[:, trix] = yp\n660\t                    \n661\t                except:\n662\t                    continue\n663\t            \n664\t            # load_motion_energy(f, me_file, goCue, Ntrials):\n705\t    \"\"\"Load and align motion energy to neural time axis.\n706\t    \n707\t    Matches loadMotionEnergy.m.\n708\t    Returns: (n_timebins, None\n780\t\n781\t\n782\tdef discretize_continuous(values_per_trial, threshold_percentile=50):\n783\t    \"\"\"Discretize continuous time-varying values into 2 bins using per-session threshold.\n784\t    \n785\t    Args:\n786\t        values_per_trial: list of 1D arrays (time-varying values per trial)\n787\t        threshold_percentile: percentile for threshold (50 = median)\n788\t    \n789\t    Returns:\n790\t        list of 1D arrays with values 0 or 1 (as float32)\n791\t    \"\"\"\n792\t    # Compute threshold from all valid values across all trials\n793\t    all_values = np.concatenate([v.flatten() for v in values_per_trial])\n794\t    all_values = all_values[~np.isnan(all_values)]\n795\t    \n796\t    if len(all_values) == 0:\n797\t        return [np.zeros_like(v, dtype=np.float32) for v in values_per_trial]\n798\t    \n799\t    threshold = np.percentile(all_values, threshold_percentile)\n800\t    \n801\t    # Handle edge case: if threshold is 0 (e.g., tongue velocity is mostly 0\n802\t    # when tongue is not visible), use median of positive values instead\n803\t    if threshold == 0:\n804\t        pos_values = all_values[all_values > 0]\n805\t        if len(pos_values) > 0:\n806\t            threshold = np.percentile(pos_values, threshold_percentile)\n807\t    \n808\t    result = []\n809\t    for v in values_per_trial:\n810\t        disc = (v >= threshold).astype(np.float32)\n811\t        result.append(disc)\n812\t    \n813\t    return result\n814\t\n815\t\n816\tdef plot_processing(session_result, session_idx):\n817\t    \"\"\"Plot processing velocity = gradient(position), NaN -> 0\n        xvel = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), dtype=np.float64)\n        yvel = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        for trix in range(Ntrials):\n            xv = np.gradient(xpos[:, trix])\n            yv = np.gradient(ypos[:, trix])\n            # For tongue: set NaN velocity to 0\n            xv[np.isnan(xv)] = 0\n            yv[np.isnan(yv)] = 0\n            xvel[:, trix] = xv\n            yvel[:, trix] = yv\n        \n        # Compute speed (magnitude of velocity)\n        speed = np.sqrt(xvel**2 + yvel**2)\n        \n        return speed\n        \n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f'    Warning: Could not compute tongue velocity: {e}')\n        return None\n\n\ndef compute_paw_velocity(f, goCue, Ntrials):\n    \"\"\"Compute paw velocity from DLC top view data.\n    \n    Uses view 2 (index 1), features 'top_paw' and 'bottom_paw'.\n    Returns: (n_timebins, Ntrials) array of paw speed, or None.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        traj_ref = f['obj']['traj'][1, 0]  # view 2 (top)\n        traj_group = f[traj_ref]\n        \n        taxis = TIME_AXIS + PARAMS['advance_movement']\n        vidshift = find_video_offset(f)\n        \n        # Find paw feature indices\n        feat_ref = traj_group['featNames'][0, 0]\n        feat_data = f[feat_ref]\n        feat_names = []\n        for j in range(feat_data.shape[1]):\n            ref = feat_data[0, j]\n            chars = f[ref][:].flatten()\n            feat_names.append(''.join(chr(c) for c in chars))\n        \n        paw_indices = []\n        for i, name in enumerate(feat_names):\n            if 'paw' in name.lower():\n                paw_indices.append(i)\n        \n        if len(paw_indices) == 0:\n            print('    Warning: paw features not found in view 2')\n            return None\n        \n        # Average velocity across paw features\n        all_speeds = []\n        \n        for paw_idx in paw_indices:\n            xpos = np.full((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float64)\n            ypos = np.full((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float64)\n            \n            for trix in range(Ntrials):\n                try:\n                    ts_ref = traj_group['ts'][trix, 0]\n                    ts_data = f[ts_ref][:]\n                    \n                    ndrop_ref = traj_group['NdroppedFrames'][trix, 0]\n                    ndrop = f[ndrop_ref][:].flatten()\n                    if np.isnan(ndrop).any():\n                        continue\n                    \n                    try:\n                        ft_ref = traj_group['frameTimes'][trix, 0]\n                        frameTimes = f[ft_ref][:].flatten()\n                    except:\n                        n_frames = ts_data.shape[-1] if ts_data.ndim == 3 else ts_data.shape[0]\n                        frameTimes = np.arange(1, n_frames + 1) / 400.0\n                    \n                    if np.all(np.isnan(frameTimes)):\n                        continue\n                    \n                    # Extract x, y for paw\n                    if ts_data.ndim == 3:\n                        if ts_data.shape[0] == len(feat_names):\n                            x = ts_data[paw_idx, 0, :]\n                            y = ts_data[paw_idx, 1, :]\n                        elif ts_data.shape[2] == len(feat_names):\n                            x = ts_data[:, 0, paw_idx]\n                            y = ts_data[:, 1, paw_idx]\n                        else:\n                            x = ts_data[paw_idx, 0, :]\n                            y = ts_data[paw_idx, 1, :]\n                    else:\n                        continue\n                    \n                    aligned_times = frameTimes - vidshift - goCue[trix]\n                    \n                    from scipy.interpolate import interp1d\n                    valid = ~np.isnan(aligned_times)\n                    if np.sum(valid) < 2:\n                        continue\n                    \n                    # For non-tongue: smooth with window 1 (no-op) and fill missing\n                    fx = interp1d(aligned_times[valid], x[valid], bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)\n                    fy = interp1d(aligned_times[valid], y[valid], bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)\n                    xp = fx(taxis)\n                    yp = fy(taxis)\n                    \n                    # Fill missing with nearest\n                    mask = ~np.isnan(xp)\n                    if np.any(mask):\n                        from scipy.interpolate import interp1d as interp1d_fill\n                        indices = np.arange(len(xp))\n                        xp = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], xp[mask])\n                    mask = ~np.isnan(yp)\n                    if np.any(mask):\n                        yp = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], yp[mask])\n                    \n                    xpos[:, trix] = xp\n                    ypos[:, trix] = yp\n                    \n                except:\n                    continue\n            \n            # Compute velocity\n            xvel = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), dtype=np.float64)\n            yvel = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), dtype=np.float64)\n            \n            for trix in range(Ntrials):\n                xv = np.gradient(xpos[:, trix])\n                yv = np.gradient(ypos[:, trix])\n                \n                # For non-tongue: subtract baseline derivative and fill missing\n                basederiv_x = np.nanmedian(np.diff(xpos[:, trix]))\n                basederiv_y = np.nanmedian(np.diff(ypos[:, trix]))\n                if not np.isnan(basederiv_x):\n                    xv = xv - basederiv_x\n                if not np.isnan(basederiv_y):\n                    yv = yv - basederiv_y\n                \n                # Fill missing\n                mask = ~np.isnan(xv)\n                if np.any(mask):\n                    indices = np.arange(len(xv))\n                    xv = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], xv[mask])\n                mask = ~np.isnan(yv)\n                if np.any(mask):\n                    yv = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], yv[mask])\n                \n                xvel[:, trix] = xv\n                yvel[:, trix] = yv\n            \n            speed = np.sqrt(xvel**2 + yvel**2)\n            all_speeds.append(speed)\n        \n        # Average across paw features\n        avg_speed = np.mean(all_speeds, axis=0)\n        return avg_speed\n        \n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f'    Warning: Could not compute paw velocity: {e}')\n        return None\n\n\ndef load_motion_energy(f, me_file, goCue, Ntrials):\n    \"\"\"Load and align motion energy to neural time axis.\n    \n    Matches loadMotionEnergy.m.\n    Returns: (n_timebins, Ntrials) array, or None.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not os.path.exists(me_file):\n        print(f'    Warning: Motion energy file not found: {me_file}')\n        return None\n    \n    try:\n        import scipy.io as sio\n        me_raw = sio.loadmat(me_file)\n        me_struct = me_raw['me'][0, 0]\n        me_data = me_struct['data']\n        # Handle nested struct: if me.data is itself a struct with 'data' field\n        # (matching MATLAB: if isstruct(me.data), me.data = me.data.data)\n        if me_data.dtype.names is not None and 'data' in me_data.dtype.names:\n            me_data = me_data[0, 0]['data']\n        # me_data should now be (Ntrials, 1) object array\n        \n        taxis = TIME_AXIS + PARAMS['advance_movement']\n        vidshift = find_video_offset(f)\n        \n        me_aligned = np.zeros((N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials), dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        for trix in range(min(Ntrials, me_data.shape[0])):\n            try:\n                me_trial = me_data[trix, 0].flatten()  # motion energy time series\n                \n                # Get frameTimes from traj\n                try:\n                    traj_ref = f['obj']['traj'][0, 0]\n                    traj_group = f[traj_ref]\n                    ft_ref = traj_group['frameTimes'][trix, 0]\n                    frameTimes = f[ft_ref][:].flatten()\n                except:\n                    frameTimes = np.arange(1, len(me_trial) + 1) / 400.0\n                \n                if np.all(np.isnan(frameTimes)) or len(frameTimes) == 0:\n                    frameTimes = np.arange(1, len(me_trial) + 1) / 400.0\n                \n                # Align times\n                aligned_times = frameTimes - vidshift - goCue[trix]\n                \n                # Truncate to match lengths\n                min_len = min(len(aligned_times), len(me_trial))\n                aligned_times = aligned_times[:min_len]\n                me_trial = me_trial[:min_len]\n                \n                # Interpolate to neural time axis\n                valid = ~np.isnan(aligned_times) & ~np.isnan(me_trial)\n                if np.sum(valid) < 2:\n                    continue\n                \n                from scipy.interpolate import interp1d\n                f_interp = interp1d(aligned_times[valid], me_trial[valid], \n                                   bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)\n                me_interp = f_interp(taxis)\n                \n                # Fill NaN with nearest\n                mask = ~np.isnan(me_interp)\n                if np.any(mask):\n                    indices = np.arange(len(me_interp))\n                    me_interp = np.interp(indices, indices[mask], me_interp[mask])\n                \n                me_aligned[:, trix] = me_interp\n                \n            except Exception as e:\n                continue\n        \n        return me_aligned\n        \n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f'    Warning: Could not load motion energy: {e}')\n        return None\n\n\ndef discretize_continuous(values_per_trial, threshold_percentile=50):\n    \"\"\"Discretize continuous time-varying values into 2 bins using per-session threshold.\n    \n    Args:\n        values_per_trial: list of 1D arrays (time-varying values per trial)\n        threshold_percentile: percentile for threshold (50 = median)\n    \n    Returns:\n        list of 1D arrays with values 0 or 1 (as float32)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Compute threshold from all valid values across all trials\n    all_values = np.concatenate([v.flatten() for v in values_per_trial])\n    all_values = all_values[~np.isnan(all_values)]\n    \n    if len(all_values) == 0:\n        return [np.zeros_like(v, dtype=np.float32) for v in values_per_trial]\n    \n    threshold = np.percentile(all_values, threshold_percentile)\n    \n    # Handle edge case: if threshold is 0 (e.g., tongue velocity is mostly 0\n    # when tongue is not visible), use median of positive values instead\n    if threshold == 0:\n        pos_values = all_values[all_values > 0]\n        if len(pos_values) > 0:\n            threshold = np.percentile(pos_values, threshold_percentile)\n    \n    result = []\n    for v in values_per_trial:\n        disc = (v >= threshold).astype(np.float32)\n        result.append(disc)\n    \n    return result\n\n\ndef plot_processing(session_result, session_idx):\n    \"\"\"Plot ============================================================\n# MAIN CONVERSION\n# ============================================================\n\ndef main():\n    parser = How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Defensively and silently. (1) `warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')` at import. (2) Every per-trial camera/motion-energy computation is wrapped in `try/except: continue`, and each of the three top-level camera functions is wrapped in a `try/except` that prints a warning and returns `None`. (3) When a stream returns `None`, the session's trials get all-zero arrays for that output; when a single trial fails, its column stays zero. Zeros are then discretised as \"low\", so missing video is indistinguishable from genuinely low movement. (4) Untracked tongue frames (NaN positions) become velocity 0; untracked paw/motion-energy bins are filled by linear interpolation. (5) `NdroppedFrames` containing NaN causes the trial's tracking to be skipped. (6) Structural variability is handled: `ts` orientation is detected from `featNames` length, dual- vs single-probe `clu` layouts, nested `me.data` structs, clusters with empty/null quality strings. (7) Sessions missing a data file, having <2 valid trials, or <10 neurons are skipped. Not handled: trials after the end of the ephys recording (these would appear as all-zero firing across all neurons), and `bp` fields longer than `Ntrials`.\n\nii.\n```python\nwarnings.filterwarnings('ignore')\n```\n```python\n            except Exception as e:\n                continue\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f'    Warning: Could not compute tongue velocity: {e}')\n        return None\n```\n```python\n        if tongue_vel is not None:\n            tongue_vel_trials.append(tongue_vel[:, trial_idx].astype(np.float32))\n        else:\n            tongue_vel_trials.append(np.zeros(N_TIMEBINS, dtype=np.float32))\n```\n```python\n                ndrop = f[ndrop_ref][:].flatten()\n                if np.isnan(ndrop).any():\n                    continue\n```\n\niii. The AI reports only whole-session timings (`t_start`/`elapsed` per session), 4–16 s per session and 188.9 s for the 25-session run, and does not profile within a session. The actual dominant cost is the neural block: a Python loop over clusters × all `Ntrials` trials that performs one `np.histogram` **and one `scipy.signal.convolve`** per (cluster, trial) — roughly 1.6 M convolutions over the dataset — on top of one HDF5 read of `trialtm`, `trial` and (unused) `tm` per cluster. Second is the camera block: three passes over all trials with a fresh `interp1d` per trial per feature. For comparison the human reference converts 44 sessions in ~135 s; the AI takes 189 s for 25.\n\nii.\n```python\n        for ci, clu_idx in enumerate(cluid):\n            ...\n            for trial_num in range(1, Ntrials + 1):\n                ...\n                counts, _ = np.histogram(trial_spikes, bins=EDGES)\n                fr = counts / PARAMS['dt']\n                fr_smooth = causal_gaussian_smooth(fr, PARAMS['smooth'], PARAMS['bctype'])\n```\n```python\n    elapsed = time.time() - t_start\n    print(f'    Done: {n_neurons} neurons, {len(valid_trials)} trials, {elapsed:.1f}s')\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 7 Run Time Estimates: \"Full processing | ~6-7s | ~180s (25 sessions)\", i.e. the AI's justification is simply that the total is far under the 15-minute budget in the instructions, so no optimisation was pursued. No speed-ups are listed in the Step 6 \"Code speedups added\" section.\n\n## 11-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Nothing was vectorised. The clearly vectorisable loops that remain are: (1) the `for trial_num in range(1, Ntrials+1)` spike-binning loop, which is a single `np.histogram2d(spike_trial, spike_aligned, bins=[trial_edges, EDGES])` over all trials at once (as in the reference); (2) the per-trial smoothing call, since the whole `(time, trials)` matrix could be filtered in one call along axis 0; (3) the per-column `for j in range(x_padded.shape[1])` convolution loop inside `causal_gaussian_smooth`; (4) the per-trial `np.gradient` loops in `compute_tongue_velocity` and `compute_paw_velocity`, which operate on rectangular `(N_TIMEBINS, Ntrials)` arrays and could be single `np.gradient(..., axis=0)` calls; (5) the baseline-derivative and NaN-fill loops, likewise. The per-trial interpolation loops are the only ones genuinely hard to vectorise, because each trial has a different number of camera frames.\n\nii.\n```python\n    for trix in range(Ntrials):\n        xv = np.gradient(xpos[:, trix])\n        yv = np.gradient(ypos[:, trix])\n        xv[np.isnan(xv)] = 0\n        yv[np.isnan(yv)] = 0\n        xvel[:, trix] = xv\n        yvel[:, trix] = yv\n```\n```python\n    for j in range(x_padded.shape[1]):\n        result[:, j] = convolve(x_padded[:, j], kern, mode='same')\n```\n\niii. Not discussed. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 6 leaves \"Code inefficiencies identified\" and \"Code speedups added\" effectively empty, and the Step 7 estimate (~180 s) was used to conclude no optimisation was needed.\n\n## 11-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. Four repetitions. (1) `find_video_offset(f)` is called three times per session — once in `compute_tongue_velocity`, once in `compute_paw_velocity`, once in `load_motion_energy` — each time re-reading `bp.ev.bitStart` and `sglx.bitcode.bitstart` and computing two modes, although the offset is a session constant; it also computes `np.median(bitStart)` and immediately overwrites it.
